requiredFindings.title: Bound descriptor service so traffic cannot starve deadlines
requiredFindings.detail: service_stderr loops until EOF or a read error, and service_control (1085-1123) loops across complete frames until a read returns Pending. Neither has a per-turn work bound or checks a deadline. A continuously replenished stderr pipe or control stream can keep one call running indefinitely, preventing participant I/O, timers, ladder advancement and settlement. The fixed buffer bounds storage, not service time. The existing finite stderr flood does not prove fairness. The trigger receiver drain at 819 has the same issue if producers continually refill it.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Bound reads/frames/trigger consumption per turn and return to the merged loop so every ready end, timer and teardown step gets service under sustained input. Retain resumable acquisition and fixed stderr storage. Add sustained-producer or deterministic always-ready controls proving wall-clock/liveness/ladder deadlines and participant service still advance.

requiredFindings.title: Give a clean end a finite reap ceiling
requiredFindings.detail: check_clean sets first_cause=Clean and state=Reaping without creating a ladder (1392-1400). If try_reap keeps returning None or an error, reap_step can expire only a ladder.kill_at deadline, which is absent. The terminal disables the wall clock; the normal grace merely marks grace_expired when Done and shutdown_ack are true. Consequently a fully joined normal end with the existing reap_blocked seam never settles. The comment that a clean end gets a ceiling is not implemented; the unreapable-root control uses the fault path only.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Start and track a finite reap deadline for the clean path, include it in next_deadline, append ReapCeiling on expiry and abandon without further signalling or blocking. Add the normal clean script with reap_blocked and prove finite single settlement, exit=unreaped and no admissible output.

requiredFindings.title: Stop EINTR retries when the readiness deadline expires
requiredFindings.detail: wait_ready recomputes a saturating remaining timeout, but every EINTR unconditionally continues (1954-1955), including after the deadline when the timeout has become zero. Repeated interruptions can therefore retain the readiness call beyond its stated bound and keep the supervisor from enforcing its own deadlines. The new platform test exercises timeout/readiness/hang-up, not interrupted waits.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: On EINTR, check the original absolute deadline and return a timeout result once it has expired; preserve zero-timeout sampling and clear readiness outputs appropriately. Add an injected repeated-EINTR control that crosses the deadline and terminates finitely.

requiredFindings.title: Retain shutdown until a pending control write completes
requiredFindings.detail: reach_terminal makes 64 immediate flush attempts, then calls send_control(shutdown) once and ignores its false result. If a prior control frame is still pending after short writes, WouldBlock or interruptions, send_control refuses because control_out is nonempty (791). close_fd3_after_write then closes fd3 after that older frame drains. No shutdown is queued or retried, so a valid terminal can be turned into a missing-shutdownAck deadline through host-side write scheduling. The comment that shutdown waits for the pending write is not implemented.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Track the pending normal shutdown explicitly and send it through ControlSession::send once the older frame completes, retaining its bytes/offset across readiness turns. Close fd3 only after shutdown itself is written (or an actual fault/expiry). Add a control-write backpressure/short-write case where terminal arrives with an older frame pending and assert exactly one shutdown and clean completion.

requiredFindings.title: Resolve additions to the closed settlement content before acceptance
requiredFindings.detail: ScratchFate adds KeptWithUnreapedRoot and NoScratch, and Settlement.exit is optional (around 277), as Q-D3A1-1 and Q-D3A1-4 disclose. Item 12 closes scratch to removed/retained; accepted LD-D3A-17 adds only io-failure and work-exhausted retention reasons. It does not authorize either new fate or an absent exit. These public settlement states are produced now, including in tests; future D3a-3 projection does not supply authority for them. Preserving an unreaped root's custody is sound, but the representation is unresolved.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Obtain an explicit narrow law/plan amendment for unreaped-root retention and the nothing-spawned case, or select an authorized representation before accepting this settlement API. Align public types, settlement construction and tests. Do not mislabel a still-held scratch as removed, invent errno/work exhaustion, or label a process that never existed as unreaped.

requiredFindings.title: Preserve the required liveness classification for a nonce mismatch
requiredFindings.detail: Every local refused frame is mapped to ControlRefusal(family). D2a rejects a mismatched healthReport nonce as RF7 (control_protocol.rs:1416-1420), so the implementation never emits LivenessMissed or cause=Liveness for that case. Item 15 explicitly classifies missing or mismatched health reports as liveness faults. This is Q-D3A1-2 and changes the settlement cause and required event, not just diagnostics. RF7 also covers unrelated sequence/state errors, so remapping every RF7 would be incorrect.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Retain precise typed provenance for the health-nonce mismatch from the control owner and project that case to LivenessMissed/cause=Liveness, while retaining the protocol refusal evidence and ordinary RF7 handling for other violations. Alternatively obtain an explicit governing amendment. Add matching busy, mismatched nonce and unrelated RF7 controls.

requiredFindings.title: Resolve the cause of an accepted control fault frame
requiredFindings.detail: An accepted control fault directly triggers ProviderProtocol even when the participant has never reached FAULT. Item 12 defines that closed cause as the participant reaching FAULT, and this implementation neither advances the participant to FAULT nor records an authorized extension of the cause. Q-D3A1-3 correctly identifies the gap. An accepted control fault is also distinct from a refused control frame.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Record the owning law decision for this boundary report and implement its authorized cause/transition. If provider-protocol is intended to include accepted control fault reports, explicitly amend that definition and add a control-fault fixture asserting the cause, unchanged provider bytes and protocol-owned process events. Do not invent a new participant process event or deadline for this non-deadline teardown.

requiredFindings.title: Keep an independently observed early death as a later trigger
requiredFindings.detail: append_death suppresses UnexpectedExit whenever any first cause already exists. In particular, the exit source is serviced first: a natural early exit can be observed before fd1 EOF triggers ProviderProtocol, and its death is appended only after the J-3 drain. At that point the explicit first_cause.is_none guard drops UnexpectedExit. Item 12 requires later triggers to be appended and kept. Q-D3A1-5's concern about host-caused deaths does not justify dropping a death already observed before the host signalled the group.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Retain sufficient ordering/provenance to distinguish an independently observed early death from ladder-caused death. Keep the EOF-induced ProviderProtocol first when that is the earlier appended trigger, and append UnexpectedExit later for the known independent early death. Preserve J-3 delivery order and deliver host-caused death only as its real protocol event. Add controls for exit observed before EOF/teardown, fd1 held past drain and host-caused death.

requiredFindings.title: Capture the tree confirmation while the root is still unreaped
requiredFindings.detail: The successful fault path calls try_reap and then settle (1525-1526). settle computes the killed tree report with root_alone, which requires group_members to contain exactly the root pid (1510-1517). After reaping that zombie, the ordinary root-only group is empty, so a successful teardown is reported Incomplete rather than GroupKilledPlatformLimited. LD-D3A-6 requires confirmation against the zombie root alone; that observation has been lost. The tests inspect exit and scratch but do not assert this report.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Capture and retain the authorized group confirmation before reaping, with the root identity still held, and derive the settlement report from that observation. Do not signal or perform a by-pid confirmation after reap. Test both a root-only killed group and a group that remains nonempty/incomplete.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Late-trigger coverage currently depends on a private extra turn
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The late-event test manually calls private turn() after settlement. Public run() returns as soon as Settled; its handle still accepts triggers while the receiver lives, so those later sends are not automatically counted/dropped. Make the public lifecycle guarantee explicit before J2 composition.
nonBlockingObservations.suggestedChange: Either close/reject handle sends at settlement or arrange a bounded late-event accounting mechanism; test the public lifecycle rather than relying solely on an extra private turn.
